Please act as a professional Verilog designer. Your task is to create a Verilog module that implements an FFT (Fast Fourier Transform) block and an IFFT (Inverse Fast Fourier Transform) block. 
An FFT is an algorithm that computes the discrete Fourier transform (DFT) of a sequence, which is a mathematical operation that transforms a time-domain signal into a frequency-domain signal. The IFFT is the inverse operation of the FFT, which transforms a frequency-domain signal back into a time-domain signal. 

The inputs to the FFT block are a set of complex numbers, and the output is the DFT of the input sequence. The inputs to the IFFT block are the DFT of a sequence, and the output is the sequence in the time domain. 

Your module should have the following inputs and outputs:

Inputs: a set of n complex numbers (real and imaginary parts)
Outputs: a set of n complex numbers (real and imaginary parts)

The module should also have the following parameters:

n: the length of the input sequence (must be a power of 2)
twiddle_bits: the number of bits used to represent the twiddle factors (must be an integer)

Your module should implement the following functionality:

The FFT block should compute the DFT of the input sequence using the Cooley-Tukey algorithm, which is an efficient algorithm that reduces the number of computations required to compute the DFT. 
The IFFT block should compute the inverse DFT of the input sequence using the same algorithm as the FFT block, but with the conjugate of the twiddle factors. 

To implement the FFT and IFFT blocks, you should use Verilog code to define the twiddle factors as complex numbers, and compute the DFT and IDFT using the Cooley-Tukey algorithm. You should also use butterfly modules to perform the computations at each stage of the algorithm. 

You may use the following butterfly module for the computations:

module butterfly (
    input wire [1:0] select, // select bit
    input wire [twiddle_bits-1:0] tw_re, // twiddle factor real part
    input wire [twiddle_bits-1:0] tw_im, // twiddle factor imaginary part

    input wire [1:0] input_im, // input imaginary part
    output wire [1:0] output_re, // output real part
    output wire [1:0] output_im // output imaginary part
);
